# identify_whitelisted_barcodes.R

## identify_whitelisted_barcodes()

We have moved the code for reading in the whitelisted barcode files (`75K_barcode.csv`, `Wong_barcode_pairs.csv`) and the `cell_to_extracted_BCs.rds` outside of the `identify_whitelisted_barcodes()` function. It is displayed below for posterity.

```{r}
identify_whitelisted_barcodes(
  source_dir = "data",
  BC1_whitelist_file_name = "75K_barcode.csv",
  BC2_BC3_whitelist_file_name = "Wong_barcode_pairs.csv",
  cell_to_extracted_BCs_file_name = "cell_to_extracted_BCs.rds",
  output_dir = "data",
  verbose = TRUE
)
```

Performing `identify_whitelisted_barcodes()` on the original data is exceptionally slow. A subsetted version of our data is produced below, and is used in the example provided for this function.

```{r}
# Subset 200 of the 75987 whitelist barcodes
BC1_whitelist <- read.table("data/75K_barcode.csv", sep = ",")$V1
BC1_whitelist_subset <- sample(BC1_whitelist, 200)

df <- data.frame(barcode = BC1_whitelist_subset)
readr::write_csv(df, "data/75K_barcode_subset.csv", col_names = FALSE)

# Subset 1000 rows of the cell_to_extracted_BCs data frame (originally 60677 obs.)
cell_to_extracted_BCs <- readRDS("data/cell_to_extracted_BCs.rds")
cell_to_extracted_BCs_subset <- cell_to_extracted_BCs[sample(nrow(cell_to_extracted_BCs), 1000), ]
saveRDS(cell_to_extracted_BCs_subset, file = "data/cell_to_extracted_BCs_subset.rds")
```

```{r}
identify_whitelisted_barcodes(
  source_dir = "data",
  BC1_whitelist_file_name = "75K_barcode_subset.csv",
  BC2_BC3_whitelist_file_name = "Wong_barcode_pairs.csv",
  cell_to_extracted_BCs_file_name = "cell_to_extracted_BCs_subset.rds",
  output_dir = "data",
  verbose = FALSE
)
```
